answer: Bind every agent identity to a hardware-backed key sealed in a TEE, so spawning identities on one box gets expensive. New accounts start weightless and gain influence only through endorsements from established, non-kin peers; these endorsements interlock like a trellis, so a single attacker clique cannot prop up many fakes. Publish an atlas of the endorsement graph: subgraphs showing near-clique symmetry or uniform timing are quarantined. Limit the trust horizon so endorsements decay after N epochs, forcing continuous honest participation. Sybils become costly to create and hard to hide.
